Variance decomposition of the vibration of effects

Source: R/voe.R
voe_variance.Rd

Regresses estimate on the specification decisions (as factors) and reports, for each decision \(d\), the unique R-squared $$R^2_{\mathrm{u}}(d) = R^2_{\mathrm{full}} - R^2_{-d},$$ where \(R^2_{\mathrm{full}}\) is the R-squared of the model with all the decisions and \(R^2_{-d}\) the one without \(d\), separately for each response x coefficient. With a complete, balanced grid of specifications and no interactions, the unique R-squared equals the ANOVA share of variance (Klau et al. 2023) .

Usage

voe_variance(
  x,
  estimate = "pcor",
  p.adjusted = NULL,
  focal = NULL,
  which.response = NULL,
  focal.var = NULL
)

Arguments

x

a pima object, a pima.multi object created with fit.specs, a list of fitted lm or glm models, or a table returned by spec_table().

estimate

column of the specification table to decompose.

p.adjusted

not used: p-values play no role in the decomposition. Kept for backward compatibility; when not NULL it is only checked with the rules of voe().

focal, focal.var

coefficients and variables to consider, as in spec_curve(); by default the tested coefficients (pima), the focal predictors (pima.multi) or all the coefficients except the intercept. Each selected coefficient is a separate association.

which.response

responses to consider; defaults to all.

Value

A list with r2 (one row per response x coefficient) and dec (one row per response x coefficient x decision, with source equal to "predictor" or "other", and r2u_inclusion, r2u_transformation for predictors).

Details

Decisions are the predictors (attr(spec_table(x), "spec_predictors"), one factor per predictor whose levels are the terms used to include it and "<predictor> (removed)" when it is excluded) and the other specification choices (the remaining attr(spec_table(x), "spec_vars"), e.g. subset, fit_spec, family, link). Decisions that do not vary within an association are dropped, and so are decisions that define the same partition of the specifications as an earlier one (e.g. link when it is fully determined by fit_spec). A decision nested in another one (e.g. link with fewer levels than fit_spec) is kept, but its unique R-squared is 0 by construction.

For predictor decisions the unique R-squared is also split into two nested parts that sum to it: r2u_inclusion (removed vs included, whatever the form) and r2u_transformation (variation among the forms of an included predictor). Both are NA for the other decisions.

References

Klau S, Schönbrodt FD, Patel CJ, Ioannidis JPA, Boulesteix A, Hoffmann S (2023). “Comparing the Vibration of Effects due to Model, Data Pre-Processing and Sampling Uncertainty on a Large Data Set in Personality Psychology.” Meta-Psychology, 7. doi:10.15626/MP.2020.2556 .

See also

Other vibration of effects: janus(), voe(), volcano()

Examples

multi <- create_multi(
  Sepal.Width ~ Sepal.Length + Petal.Width + Species,
  data = iris,
  focal = "Sepal.Length",
  nfuns = "log",
  fit.specs = list(lm = lm)
)
voe_variance(multi, estimate = "estimate")
#> $r2
#>      response  coefficient        r2     r2.adj
#> 1 Sepal.Width Sepal.Length 0.4855382 -0.2861545
#> 
#> $dec
#>      response  coefficient        term    source       r2u      pr2u
#> 1 Sepal.Width Sepal.Length Petal.Width predictor 0.2948403 0.6072443
#> 2 Sepal.Width Sepal.Length     Species predictor 0.1906979 0.3927557
#>   r2u_inclusion r2u_transformation
#> 1     0.2790126         0.01582772
#> 2     0.1906979         0.00000000
#>
